claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve full densification.
Single-phase ZrB2 has strong Zr–B and B–B interactions.
ZrB2 processed at reduced temperatures has limited oxidation resistance.
ZrB2 processed at reduced temperatures has limited liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Adding Hf-, Nb-, Ti-, and Ta-diborides to ZrB2 can produce a single-phase high-entropy AlB2-type diboride solid solution.
High-energy mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering is a viable fabrication route for the proposed class of high-entropy metal diborides.
The proposed doped ZrB2 can achieve full densification at approximately 1700 °C.
The high-entropy constituents will be homogeneously distributed within the boride lattice.
High-entropy doping will produce a refined microstructure with uniform grain boundaries.
The high-entropy mixture enhances diffusion kinetics during sintering.
Dopant-induced lattice distortion and strain disrupt diffusion barriers and enhance mass transport at lower temperatures.
Configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase diboride structure.
The multiple refractory components form protective mixed oxides during service.
The proposed protective mixed oxides retard high-temperature oxidation.
The proposed protective mixed oxides minimize liquid-metal corrosion.
The doped material will have hardness comparable to or greater than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The doped material will have fracture strength comparable to or greater than conventional high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The doped material will have superior oxidation resistance relative to both high-temperature-sintered pure ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
The doped material will have superior liquid-plating-metal durability relative to both high-temperature-sintered pure ZrB2 and earlier low-temperature specimens.
